neighbours.label: Computational data-analysis vocabulary (microarray datasets, search tools, bioinformatics software, clustering code) in life-science methods text
fire: Raw reads were aligned with BWA and variants were called using standard bioinformatics data analysis pipelines.
We downloaded microarray datasets from public repositories and clustered them with MiniBatchKMeans.
Protein interactions were predicted with the Search Tool for the Retrieval of Interacting Genes.
Differential expression analysis was performed in R using the limma package on normalized counts.
Text mining of the full life sciences literature was used to extract gene-disease relationships.
Sequencing data were uploaded into bioinformatics software for pathway enrichment analysis.
Gene ontology terms were assigned with a BLAST search against the reference database.
The script filters reads with re.search before mapping them to the reference genome.
quiet: Raw tissue samples were frozen in liquid nitrogen and stored at minus eighty degrees.
We collected lung tissue from mice and stained the sections with hematoxylin and eosin.
Protein bands were separated by gel electrophoresis and transferred onto a membrane.
Cells were grown in culture medium supplemented with ten percent fetal bovine serum.
Mice were housed in standard cages with free access to food and water for two weeks.
Blood samples were centrifuged and the plasma was kept on ice until further use.
Leaves were harvested at dawn and washed twice in sterile water before extraction.
The tubes were incubated overnight at thirty-seven degrees on a gentle shaker.

notes: Card: no single token; top examples are in bioinformatics/computational biology text (MiniBatch, Search Tool, microarray repositories, data analysis software). Near misses are wet-lab methods text.
